title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: bucket Cheon v5 (the accepted lead's own slack with every schedule and price a worst-case bound: dependent-recurrence gap tables with own inversions, closed pool representation, corrected C7)

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 target with auxiliary powers and every n with 2^20 <= n < r, the deterministic algorithm in proof.md recovers s with heuristic success probability at least 0.395 (at least 0.39 required). The success argument is the accepted lineage's law-based argument restated: 1 - e^{-K} = 0.39950 at the lower bound K = 0.51 (the realised 6N^2/m is 0.51 x (1 + 2^-54.2), N = 65196422678611482903494932429799424 = 2^64 x L exactly) under H1, minus the eight cap tails C1-C8 (each computed here from scratch, every tail rounded towards the larger probability, together charged 2^-40) minus the 2^-20 C8 modelling budget. C4 and C6 carry the routing/slot conditioning (false candidates N^2/2^192 = 2^39.30, Chernoff 2^-5.7e13 at the 2^44 cap); C5 carries two channels (the off-diagonal Poisson tail exp(-1.42e7); the diagonal challenges z = a/a' at union probability 6*2^128/m = 2^-104.27); C7 is corrected to the four-further-hits bound L^5/(5!*2^768) per chain, 2^-451.7 over all chains. The walk schedule is explicit and closed: per chain the generating node builds and RETAINS the value-indexed gap table [g]Q (the affine point for every even g < 2^33, 2^32 entries at 96 bytes) by a dependent affine recurrence whose two doubling cases are priced as reference additions and whose every later entry carries its own field inversion ((2000+3830+47)/2000 per entry, since dependent recurrences cannot batch inversions); every step reads its addend from the table; rare gaps above 2^33 split against the reserve; the 2^16 lockstep segments share the table and batch their inversions; a candidate re-walk rebuilds its two chains' tables first, charged in the re-walk term. The matching representation closes: 32-byte wire records (192-bit key + 64-bit chain id), 40-byte linked pool records with 34-bit links, 5-byte head indices. Every shared price is a worst-case bound: point scalar multiplications at most 330 group operations by 4-bit fixed windows (charged 383), field inversions 10 F_r-multiplications (charged 3830) priced explicitly wherever they cannot batch, square roots as odd-part exponentiation plus the 2-adic ladder (~320 F_r-multiplications, charged 512), modexps charged 512. The cost is the exact-integer ledger W = 141260532766039631954758376738107863 target-group-operation units with records 2N x 2000 x (1 + 160/2000) and the charge 160 itemised over the 33-line six-limb listing (maximal 129/122, a 24 percent margin). Only A_1 and A_d are read, so the bound holds for every n >= 2^20. Score = ceil(10^6 log2 W)/10^6 = 116.765842, against the accepted lead's 116.793080 - a gain of 0.027238 bits, the lead's own published slack (K 0.51 versus 0.52, charge 160 versus 180 at comparable margins) net of the honest repricing.

experiments.purpose: One run, three modes. Mode ledger recomputes every size, term, cap tail, the exact integer memory sum and the exact score from integers and Fractions, asserting d | r-1, 6d | r-1, v2(r-1) = 32, the exact identity 2^64 x L = N with 6N^2/m >= 0.51, the six-limb itemisation totals (walk side 33, listing 129/122, charged 160 with a 24 percent margin) and the H-prime density sanity (402 sixteenth powers below 2^16 against 408.875 expected); it outputs W = 141260532766039631954758376738107863 units, score 116.765842, the beats-lead comparison, the walk-schedule block (the retained value-indexed gap table, the dependent-recurrence build with one own inversion per entry, the lockstep segments, the split mechanism, the re-walk rebuild), the corrected C4, the two-channel C5, the four-hits C7, the preprocessing split and the memory block (per-owner-node 480516719816 bytes with the 40-byte linked pool and 5-byte heads; per-generating-node 421595709440 bytes including the retained 2^32 x 96-byte gap table; total 2^122.806 bytes, ceiling 2^122.81). Mode coverage runs three scalar-level birthday toys (r = 134219713/536872321/2147492353 at d = 32/64/128, L = 60, chains sized for K = 0.51) measuring success against the diagonal-loss prediction 1 - e^{-K'}. Mode ec runs the whole attack end to end on the j = 0 curve y^2 = x^3 + 3 over F_207670579 of prime order r = 207671809 at d = 128: H-primes from a sieve, 15 chains of 25 steps per side with per-chain retained gap tables, the 16-bit parity key routed to 32 pseudo-nodes x 16 heads, the bucket table with the whole baby side inserted first, equal-key candidates kept as (key, id, id'), the linear re-walk with the 4-step kept cap, the six GLV/negation candidates tested against the u-twisted A_d, the recovered z divided by the eigenvalue the endomorphism actually realises on the curve (resolved at setup against P0, not assumed), the 7 square roots and the 128-root scan, asserting every recovered s equals the drawn secret. The full mode=all run completes in under 2 seconds and reproduces byte-identically from a foreign working directory.
